newsitem.title: USA: Campbell Soup rises after results.
newsitem.headline: Campbell Soup rises after results.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co shares rose Wednesday after the food company reported a rise in its earnings per share and said it would announce the divestiture of more units.
Shares in the Camden, N.J., company, the biggest U.S. maker of soups, rose 1-3/4 to 49-3/4 by mid-afternoon. Volume was moderate.
The company reported Wednesday its third quarter earnings per share were $0.34 against $0.29 for the same period last year. Net sales rose to $1.87 billion from $1.83 billion.
"It's just another great quarter, thanks to help from the gross margin side," said Erika Gritman Long, an analyst at J.P. Morgan Securities.
The margin has expanded at three percent for four straight quarters. Long cited cost-cutting efforts, increases in volume and prices and "benefits from selling low-margin businesses" for the rise.

"Their costs are remaining the same but they are getting a higher price for their product," she said, adding that Campbell remained on track for $80 million in cost savings this fiscal year and $120 million in the next.
Long said Campbell should be able to improve margins by two percent for the next year.

The company also said it expected to announce more divestitures by the end of the 1997 fiscal year. It has signed an accord to sell its Marie's salad dressing business as part of its plans to divest $500 million in non-strategic businesses over two years.
